$comment: A reference placement is REPORTED, never REQUIRED. It impeaches when it FAILS (the reference found in the protocol's native field contradicts the record) and its absence never blocks, exactly as frc-non-gating does. The `ladder` block below is the executable form of that ruling: no class may list this step. Carrier values carry the canonical 0x-prefixed sha256 form — binding-core's own decoder refuses the bare-digits form as a corrupt carrier, so a vector pinning it would certify references no conformant counterparty can read. `depth` tokens are short kebab identifiers, not prose, matching verify/authority-walk.json: they are load-bearing gap reasons a foreign implementation must reproduce, which prose could not be. THE CARRIER TYPE IS PART OF THE COMPARISON, not only the value: impeachment is reserved for a `sha256` reference naming a DIFFERENT record, because only that carrier's value IS the record fingerprint. A `url` locates and attests nothing (LCP §C.2, and binding-core.requireIntegrity refuses it) and reads `reference-not-integrity-bearing`; `ipfs`/`ar` attest to a CID this pure walk cannot re-derive and read `reference-not-a-record-fingerprint`. Both are gaps: a step required by no class can only ever pull the answer down, so every arm short of a genuine contradiction has to be one.

cases.name: extracted reference matches the record fingerprint
an UPPERCASE conformant counterparty is not false-negatived — hex is case-insensitive
extracted reference CONTRADICTS the record — impeaches
no placement supplied — a gap, never a failure
a placement slot with no extracted reference is a gap
malformed extraction reads out as a gap (steps are total)
an extracted reference with a non-string value is a gap, not a failure
no record fingerprint to compare against is a gap
same digits without the 0x prefix still PROVES — impeachment means a different record, not an odd form
cases.$comment: Both sides are normalized to the 0x form before comparison rather than stripped. A prefix difference is a CARRIER-FORM defect, and binding-core's decoder already refuses the bare-digits form upstream at extract time, so a conformant placement never emits one. Letting this step FAIL on it would drive supportedClass to TC-0 over formatting — impeaching a record whose reference names it correctly. Impeachment is reserved for a reference that names a DIFFERENT record.

cases.name: a url-typed reference is a GAP — it locates a document, it does not attest to one
cases.$comment: A CONFORMANT counterparty is enough to produce this: UCP makes links[] REQUIRED on a checkout response and names terms_of_service as its recommended type, so a merchant that placed no LCP capability at all extracts as a url through the declared discovery alias. Compared as a fingerprint that url never equals the atrHash, so a step reading the VALUE without its carrier TYPE answered failed and drove an otherwise-sound record to TC-0. A url locates and commits to nothing about content (LCP §C.2), which is why binding-core's requireIntegrity refuses it — the honest answer is a gap, never an impeachment.

cases.name: an ipfs reference is integrity-bearing but is not THIS record's fingerprint — its own gap
cases.$comment: ipfs and ar ARE content-addressed, and their value is a CID rather than the atrHash. Re-deriving one needs evidence.cidForAtrHash, which the verification walk does not depend on, so comparing the CID against the fingerprint impeaches every content-addressed reference on the wire — the same defect as the url arriving through the carrier types that are supposed to be the strong ones. Its own depth token, because 'the seller advertised a location instead of terms' and 'this verifier cannot re-derive that address' are different findings. A2A's manifest permits both types, so this is reachable today.

cases.name: an ar reference reads the same gap as ipfs — the token is about the FORM, not the network
cases.$comment: Both non-sha256 integrity carriers must read alike, or the token names one network's habit rather than the property. Impeachment stays reserved for a sha256 reference naming a DIFFERENT record.

cases.name: a reference whose type is outside the §8.2 registry is a malformed extraction
cases.$comment: The registry is closed. An unknown type is the caller's shape error and reads out under the token every other malformed extraction gets, never as one of the two carrier-class gaps — those name real properties of a real carrier.
